canonical_question: Does the stability of the single BCC phase up to 900°C imply that the alloy is free from sigma phase or topologically close-packed (TCP) phase formation in this temperature range?

question_variants.question: Does the stability of the single BCC phase up to 900°C imply that the alloy is free from sigma phase or topologically close-packed (TCP) phase formation in this temperature range?
question_variants.resolution_summary: Yes, the stability of the single BCC phase up to 900°C implies the alloy is free from sigma phase or TCP phase formation in this temperature range, as the text explicitly links the stability to the absence of secondary phases and phase decomposition.

answers.answer: The text explicitly states that the single BCC phase is stable up to 900°C, indicating excellent phase stability and implying no secondary phases (like sigma or TCP) form within this range.
answers.measurement_outcome: Single BCC solid solution stable up to 900°C.
answers.mechanism: Phase stability is maintained without decomposition into secondary phases.
evidence_spans: The microstructure of the homogenized NbTaTiV refractory HEA was characterized, using the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) backscattered electron (BSE) technique, as shown in Fig. 1A . A typical simple solid-solution HEA microstructure with grain sizes of 200 to 400 μm was identified without the presence of secondary phases or elemental segregations.

The chemical composition of the sample was verified (using the point energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy analysis) to be Nb 23.8 Ta 25.5 Ti 24.9 V 25.8 , indicating a homogeneous elemental distribution in a nearly equiatomic percentage.
The measured ND patterns of the bulk samples, as illustrated in Fig. 1B , confirm the single BCC solid solution at RT and elevated temperatures.
